newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish union rejects call for slower wage growth.
newsitem.headline: Spanish union rejects call for slower wage growth.

text.p: The secretary general of Spain's General Workers' Union rejected on Wednesday recent Bank of Spain and government comments that Spanish salaries were rising too fast.

"At the moment, some five million workers have signed agreements this year with salary rises near inflation...In addition, one cannot forget that two million state workers had their salaries frozen this year, which means that the salary rises were very moderate," general secretary Candido Mendez told Spanish national radio.
In recent days, the Economy Minister Rodrigo Rato as well as the Governor of the Bank of Spain Luis Angel Rojo urged salary moderation.
"Neither the government nor businessmen nor the Bank of Spain are fulfilling their commitments to society," Mendez said.
In the first quarter, Spanish wage inflation rose 4.2 percent a month on average, while the monthly inflation rate was 2.2 percent in March, 1.7 percent in April and 1.5 percent in May.
Mendez took particular issue with calls from employer organisation CEOE at a time when company earnings were rising.
"Corporate earnings have tripled in the last year and the Bank of Spain should push for moderating the excesses of business," he said.
He criticised the Bank of Spain for not allowing inflation moderation to have sufficient effect on the price of money.
